review_candidates.description: The Team + The Role Pendo's Technical Support Engineers are the diagnostic and strategic layer between customers and the product. This small, global team sits within Engineering and partners daily with Product, Engineering, and Customer Engineering across the US, EMEA, and APAC. The team does not operate like a help desk; it solves technical problems, strengthens customer outcomes, and turns customer signal into product insight. As a Sr. Technical Support Engineer, you will own customer issues end-to-end across Pendo's web and mobile products, from triage and debugging to resolution, documentation, and feedback loops. You will handle break/fix issues, how-to questions, configuration guidance, bug reproduction, and complex escalations while using AI tools to accelerate research, drafting, troubleshooting, and knowledge capture. At the senior level, you will also serve as a go-to technical resource for peers and contribute to the cross-functional work that makes the support function stronger. This role is based in our Raleigh office. What this looks like day-to-day Support queue ownership: You triage, diagnose, and resolve technical issues across Pendo's web and mobile products, including break/fix, how-to, best practice, and configuration questions. You manage urgency based on customer impact and own each case until the customer's problem is actually solved. Technical guidance: You provide targeted technical assistance on platform usage, configuration, and best practices for customers in your segment. Each engagement is scoped to the issue at hand, with clear resolution, documentation, and a path forward that helps the customer move independently. Customer signal: You translate customer pain into reproducible test cases, clear bug reports, and prioritized feedback for Product and Engineering. You also surface customer health signals and strategic gaps to Account Owners and Customer Success so the right teams can act. Knowledge at scale: You create and maintain internal knowledge base content so the team does not solve the same problem repeatedly. When you resolve something novel, you document it and use AI tools to draft, organize, and surface knowledge faster. Resolution follow-through: You work directly with developers on fixes and workarounds, pushing cases through to close without dropping hard problems or waiting to be chased. Customers and internal partners know where things stand because you communicate clearly and proactively. Continuous improvement: You identify recurring customer confusion, tooling gaps, workflow friction, and process issues that slow the team down. When you see a pattern, you propose the fix, write the doc, or build the internal resource that helps the team move faster. Support performance: You manage your work against resolution rate, response time, CSAT, escalation quality, and customer update expectations. Your goal is not just to respond quickly, but to resolve the real issue and reduce repeat case volume over time. Peer enablement: You help teammates navigate complex cases, share workarounds, and raise the technical bar for the support team. You make the people around you better by documenting what you learn and stepping in when others are blocked. Who You Are Beyond the qualifications, we hire through a specific lens. These aren't buzzwords; they're the things we'll actually look for in how you talk about your work. You're a builder, not a maintainer. You're most energized when there isn't a clear path yet, and you get to define it. You don't wait for direction; you identify gaps, shape solutions, and drive them forward. At Pendo, great Senior Technical Support Engineers don't just follow instructions; they operate as strategic advisors, influencing decisions, guiding stakeholders, and elevating how we work. You're AI-curious - genuinely. You're not using AI tools occasionally. You're rewiring how you work around them. You're faster, sharper, and more prolific because of it, and you bring that energy to everything — how you approach your work, how you prep, how you communicate, how you think. We want someone who sees AI as a multiplier, not a shortcut. Ability to gather and interpret useful technical details from customers, including device type, OS version, app version, screenshots, screen recordings, and logs. Active use of AI tools in daily work for research, drafting, troubleshooting, or knowledge capture, with a focus on using AI to move faster and work sharper. Comfort operating in a high-volume, unpredictable environment where priorities shift based on customer impact and you are expected to manage your own queue. Evidence of peer development, such as helping a less experienced colleague through a hard problem, proactively documenting knowledge, or taking informal ownership of a technical area. Evidence of continuous technical learning, whether formal or self-directed, with examples of what you have built, broken, or figured out. Nice-to-haves Hands-on exposure to mobile frameworks or platforms such as native iOS or Android, React Native, Flutter, or mobile SDKs.
